blocks.heading: THE IDEA
paras: One move frees the waterfront: the port and North Harbour leave for Thilafushi. Four wings then reconnect Malé to the world, the ocean, its past and its future. An amenity core of kiosks, a school and park, a sports centre and shops ties them together.

rows.text: Wing zone north, east, south and west
Wing connection to the world, the ocean, the past and the future
Amenity core node everyday needs between wings
Vista / breeze cut through the reclaimed grid to the sea

steps.title: Malé to the world
steps.kicker: EAST WING | THE HUB OF THE ATOLLS
steps.text: Every island connects through Malé. The East wing turns that traffic into a proper arrival: one terminal for ferries, airport boats and bridge buses.

steps.title: Malé to the ocean
steps.kicker: WEST WING | AN ISLAND THAT TURNED ITS BACK ON THE SEA
steps.text: Seawalls ring Malé, with only two soft edges left to the water. The West wing reopens one of them as the Ocean Hub: a beach, diving and swimming.

steps.title: Malé to its past
steps.text: Old Malé was low homes set in walled compounds, with shade, trees and air inside every plot. The South wing brings that back through breeze cuts, superblocks and pocket parks.

steps.title: Malé to its future
steps.text: Taller homes lifted on green bases, cut open with courtyards for cross-ventilation, with one plot left free as open space. The North wing’s capstone plots follow the new guidelines.
